word_classes.dm: discourse marker {D} other than you know
word_classes.yk: you know, as a discourse marker {D you know}

markup_type: nonverbal > abandoned > disfluent > backchannel > fluent (first match wins)
sentence_type: Treebank-based, parsed conversations only: complete_fluent, complete_disfluent, unfinished, response_token, fragment. parse_type is the type read off the parse; sentence_type is that type after the three utterance-level rules in refine_sentence_type

count_columns.utt_with_disfluency: utterances with a disfluent word or any part of a repair
count_columns.utt_with_filled_pause: utterances with at least one filled pause
count_columns.st_<type> / stw_<type>: utterances / words by sentence_type (blank type excluded)

speakers: A is the caller who placed the call (from_caller), B the one who answered
levels: words count in the turn where spoken; utterance counts in the turn where the utterance starts; turns sum exactly to their conversation

turns_csv.order: position of the turn in the conversation (0-based)
turns_csv.continues_previous: 1 if the turn opens by continuing an earlier utterance
turns_csv.has_disfluency / abandoned: judged from this turn's own words and marks

conversation_json.counts: conversation totals: words, utterances, turns, disfluent words, mtw / stw = words by markup_type / sentence_type

turns[].dis: 1 if the turn has a disfluency
turns[].ab: 1 if the turn has an abandoned utterance

turns[].u[].c: 1 if this piece continues an utterance from an earlier turn
turns[].u[].st: sentence_type of the whole utterance, or null
turns[].u[].ov: 1 if the utterance has an overlap mark
